sentences.text: 1  ...RESPONDENT  (BY SRI. SANJAY NAIR, ADVOCATE)

THIS CIVIL REVISION PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION  115 OF THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE, AGAINST THE ORDER  DATED 16.11.2022 PASSED ON IA IN EX.No.1764/2013 ON THE FILE  OF THE LIX ADDITIONAL CITY CIVIL JUDGE, BENGALURU,
 REJECTING THE APPLICATION FILED UNDER SECTION 47 R/W  SECTION 151 OF CPC.
 -2-  CRP No. 602 of 2022  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner herein was directed to execute the sale deed in favour of the claimant subject to the claimant depositing the balance sale consideration at Rs.310/Sq.ft., failing which, the claimant shall get the same done through a Commissioner appointed by the Court.

2. The petitioner filed an appeal under Section 34 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996 before the Commercial Court which came to be dismissed by confirming the award, against which, an appeal was preferred before this Court, the Division Bench of this Court by order dated 30.06.2022 dismissed the appeal.
3. The respondent herein filed an execution petition for executing the award passed by the sole arbitrator.

In the said proceedings, the petitioner filed an application under Section 47 of CPC,
challenging the award passed by the sole Arbitrator stating that the agreement of sale/MOU is not duly stamped.
The Execution Court dismissed the application, against which, the present petition is filed.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the award passed by the Sole Arbitrator cannot be enforced since the Memorandum of Understanding, on the basis of which the award/compensation was passed, is not sufficiently stamped as specified under Article 5(iii)(e),
Schedule IV of the Karnataka Stamp (Amendement) Act, 1995.
Hence, the execution Court has committed an error in exercising power under Section 47 of CPC.

Another, in Civil Appeal No.2845/2006.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent decree holder submits that under the Memorandum of Understanding, possession of the subject property was not handed over and the MOU is duly stamped as per Article 5(iii)(e), Schedule IV of the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act,
1995.
Hence, he submits that the Trial Court has rightly dismissed the application.
7. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

8. Perusal of the MOU indicates that the possession of the subject property was not handed over to the decree holder and was subject to the claimant depositing the balance sale consideration as per the award of the sole arbitrator.
9. The stamp duty payable on MOU as per Article 5(iii)(e) of Schedule IV of the Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1995 is Rs.200/- which is duly stamped.
Hence, the said MOU dated 24.03.2003 is sufficiently stamped.
10. Decisions relied on by the learned counsel for the petitioner is not applicable to the facts of this case.

11. Petitioner having not objected to the draft sale deed executed on 23.2.2021, could not have maintained an application under Section 47 of CPC filed on 27.5.2022 alleging that he was not provided with an opportunity to file objection to the draft sale deed.
12. I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the order passed by the Executing Court.
Accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.
